tagline: Granite markers down Highway 370, where Forrest met Sturgis.
intro: From the interpretive center on Grisham Street in Baldwyn, the byway heads west on Highway 370 to the crossroads where Nathan Bedford Forrest met Samuel Sturgis on June 10, 1864, then wanders by county roads and MS 348 down to Guntown. Baldwyn itself has the odd distinction of having been incorporated in four counties, as the county lines were redrawn around it.

Granite markers line the road and tell the battle as it goes. Forrest's cavalry beat a Federal column more than twice its size, and the fight is also called the Battle of Tishomingo Creek, for the creek named after the Chickasaw chief who once lived nearby.

moments.title: Brices Cross Roads National Battlefield Site
moments.text: A one-acre grassy park with a flagpole, a monument and two cannons marks where the Brice house stood, and more than 90 Confederate dead lie in the Old Bethany Cemetery beside it.

moments.title: Tishomingo Creek
moments.text: A footbridge stands where the wartime bridge crossed the creek, at the spot where some of the hardest fighting of the day took place.

moments.title: Guntown
moments.text: The road ends in a town named for James Gunn, a loyalist who found asylum among the Chickasaw after the Revolution.
